question: In the first national Lula-vs-Flávio-Bolsonaro runoff poll released September 17–18, 2026, what will be Lula's lead over Flávio Bolsonaro?

calls.reasoning: The outcome is one randomly-drawn poll, not the true race, so the answer is (underlying margin at ~Sep 14-17 fieldwork) + (house effect) + (sampling noise). Reference class: the ~15 national Lula-vs-Flavio runoff polls released Aug 20 - Sep 6, 2026, whose margins had median about +0.4 and mean about +0.3, with SD ~2.8. Underlying margin has narrowed steadily (mid-Jul ~+5 to +7; mid-Aug ~+3; early Sep ~0 to +1), roughly -3 pts/month, driven by Lula approval erosion since July and the STF/leak news cycle. I extrapolate a decelerating -0.5 over 12 more days (trends flatten; free TV airtime, which the Lula coalition dominates, began late August and the PT camp reports a 'novo momento'), giving an underlying margin near zero. The reported-poll distribution is mildly left-skewed: two strongly Flavio-leaning houses (Verita -5.4, Gerp -5) versus Indexa +5/+6 and AtlasIntel +4.5, while the high-cadence mainstream houses most likely to publish first in the window (Quaest, Datafolha, PoderData, Nexus/BTG, Real Time, Futura) cluster at -1 to +2. Hence median +0.5 with a mean slightly below it. Escape mass: 6% below -6 (a Verita/Gerp-class house publishing first while the Flavio drift continues is a concrete, recently-observed mechanism), 1% above +12 (requires a Flavio legal/eligibility shock plus a Lula-leaning house; nothing observed above +6 all year). Evidence is one-sided only in that no direct market or aggregator prices this specific draw, so I stay close to the recent-poll base rate.
calls.dossier:
SUBJECT: margin (Lula% minus Flavio Bolsonaro%) in the FIRST national Lula-vs-Flavio second-round voting-intention poll publicly RELEASED Sep 17-18, 2026.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the headline reported percentages of a single poll -- the first one publicly released inside the window -- as recorded in the 'Second round' table of the en.wikipedia article 'Opinion polling for the 2026 Brazilian presidential election'. NOT off a polling average, NOT off the poll with the latest fieldwork dates in the window, NOT off the Oct 4 / Oct 25 election result. Release date, not fieldwork date, governs; Wikipedia tables are ordered by fieldwork end date, so the resolver must confirm release dates externally. Raw reported percentages, not valid-vote-only recomputations. Tie-break among same-earliest-release-date polls: latest fieldwork end date, then topmost in table. Annulled if no qualifying national head-to-head poll is released in the window.

EVENT WINDOW: 2026-09-17 -> 2026-09-18 (inclusive) per the criteria; as of Now 2026-09-08T15:37Z the window has not opened, 0% elapsed, about 8.4 days until it opens. The window falls 16-17 days before the Oct 4 first round.

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: a poll margin in the low single digits, of the kind that has been published essentially every few days since late August.

BASE RATES (with the class each is computed over):
- Over ALL national Lula-vs-Flavio runoff polls released Aug 20 - Sep 6, 2026 (n approximately 15): margins ran from about -5.4 to about +6; median about +0.4; mean about +0.3; standard deviation about 2.8 (source: en/pt Wikipedia polling tables, cross-checked against Poder360 and Gazeta do Povo reporting).
- Over the SUBSET from high-cadence mainstream houses in that same window (Nexus/BTG, Datafolha, Quaest, PoderData, Real Time, Futura/Apex, AtlasIntel, Indexa, Vox): latest readings were Nexus +1 (Aug 28-30), Datafolha +2 (Sep 1-2), Quaest 0 (Sep 3-6), PoderData -1 (Aug 30 - Sep 2), Real Time 0 (Aug 27-31), Futura +0.4 (Aug 27 - Sep 1), Vox -0.6 (Aug 25-27), AtlasIntel +4.5 (Aug 25-30), Indexa +5 (Aug 20-23). Median about +0.4.
- Over the SUBSET from lower-profile / less-frequent houses in that window: Verita -5.4 (fieldwork Sep 1-4, n=3,804, MoE 2.0, TSE BR-09426/2026, released Sep 6, self-funded; source CNN Brasil), Gerp -5 (released about Aug 26; source Gazeta do Povo), Palver about 0 (source JOTA). This subset is more dispersed and skews toward Flavio.
- Over the TIME TREND of house-effect-adjusted margins: about +5 to +7 in mid-July (AtlasIntel late Jul: 49.2 vs 42.9; Datafolha/Nexus Jun-Jul: about 47-43), about +3 to +4 in mid-August (Datafolha Aug 18-20: 47-43; Nexus Aug 14-16: 47-44), about 0 to +1 in early September. Approximately -3 points per month over the last two months.

EVIDENCE, BOTH DIRECTIONS:
- Toward a more negative (pro-Flavio) reading: PoderData/Aya fieldwork Aug 30 - Sep 2, released Sep 3, was the first time since May that Flavio numerically led a runoff scenario in that series (Poder360, Sep 3). Lula's approval has eroded slowly and continuously since July; his campaign publicly attributes the tightening to an STF crisis and leaked investigations touching the president's son and a former chief of staff (ac24horas, Sep 6). Flavio's camp stated it expects to take the lead after Sep 7 (ac24horas, Sep 6). Verita (released Sep 6) reported a Flavio lead exceeding its stated 2.0-point margin of error.
- Toward a more positive (pro-Lula) reading: Datafolha fieldwork Sep 1-2, released Sep 3, still had Lula ahead. Quaest fieldwork Sep 3-6 had the two level. AtlasIntel (Aug 25-30) and Indexa (Aug 20-23) both had Lula clearly ahead. Free electoral TV airtime (horario eleitoral gratuito) began in late August; the Lula-Alckmin coalition holds the larger bloc of it, and the PT campaign describes a 'novo momento' in its internal reading (ac24horas, Sep 6). Historically, incumbent-side runoff numbers in Brazil have not moved monotonically through September.
- Pollster cadence: Brazilian national polling intensity rises sharply in the final three weeks; Nexus/BTG, PoderData, Quaest/Genial, Datafolha, Real Time Big Data, AtlasIntel, Paraná Pesquisas and numerous smaller TSE-registered houses have all published national runoff matchups in the last month, several of them weekly. Sep 17 is a Thursday and Sep 18 a Friday.
- Methodology note: sample sizes in this field run roughly 2,000-3,800; stated margins of error are typically 1.8-2.2 points on a single candidate's share, implying roughly a 2-point standard deviation on the margin from sampling alone even before house effects.

MARKETS: no prediction market or bookmaker was found that prices a poll margin on a specific release date. The Polymarket contracts surfaced by title similarity are FIRST-ROUND margin-of-victory markets closing 2026-10-04 -- different quantity (first round, not runoff), different resolution source (election result, not a poll), different date. A separate Polymarket book prices the overall presidential winner.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: any published release calendar naming which pollsters will publish on Sep 17 or Sep 18; any poll with fieldwork after Sep 6, 2026; any Kalshi/Manifold/bookmaker contract on this or a similar poll-margin question; a maintained house-effect table for the 2026 Brazilian cycle; the Agencia Lupa 'Lente nas Eleicoes #7' final-stretch analysis (HTTP 403).
calls.reference_class: Individual national second-round Lula-vs-Flavio-Bolsonaro voting-intention polls publicly released in the three weeks before the question window (Aug 20 - Sep 6, 2026; n approximately 15), measured as Lula% minus Flavio% as reported in the Wikipedia second-round table

calls.reasoning: Resolution is a single randomly-drawn poll, so the predictive distribution IS the recent cross-pollster distribution shifted for drift. Reference class (17 national Lula-v-Flavio runoff polls, fieldwork 16 Aug-7 Sep): median +0.4, mean +0.1, SD 3.1 pp. The narrowing from Lula ~+4.5 (July) to ~+0.15 (late Aug-early Sep) decelerated sharply and has plateaued over the last three weeks, so I apply only a small residual drift for Sep 12-17 fieldwork, centering at -0.3. The distribution is heavy-tailed and near-trimodal: ~20% chance the first releaser is a Flavio-leaning house (Verita/Gerp print -5 to -5.4), ~25% a Lula-leaning house (AtlasIntel/Indexa/Datafolha/CNT print +2 to +5), ~55% mainstream clustered in -1 to +1. That mixture, not race movement, sets the width. Sep 17-18 is Thu-Fri, 2.5 weeks pre-first-round with ~15 active national houses, so a qualifying poll almost certainly appears; PoderData/Aya releases on Thursdays and is one live candidate. Low-side escape (6%) is concrete: a Verita/Gerp-class house already prints -5.3/-5.4 and modest further drift pushes it past -6. High-side escape (1%) needs a Flavio collapse plus a maximally Lula-friendly house; the pool's 2026 maximum is +8.9. No market prices this question.

calls.reconciliation: Three runs centered at +0.5, -0.3 and 0.0 with near-identical widths. FACTUAL disputes: (1) the freshest datapoint - Runs 2 and 3 independently carry Nexus/BTG fieldwork Sep 4-7 released Sep 8 at Lula 45 / Flavio 46, which Run 1's dossier omits; two-source agreement on figure, fieldwork and release date settles it, and it undercuts Run 1's higher center specifically. (2) reference-class SD (2.45 vs 2.8 vs 3.1) - not a contradiction, the larger figures come from windows reaching back to mid-August when the pool was more dispersed; restricted to the recent pool ~2.6 is correct, and I carry Run 3's window forward with Run 2's Nexus datapoint added. (3) markets - all three independently confirm no contract prices a poll margin; the surfaced Polymarket books are first-round election-result margin bands (different quantity, deadline and resolution source), so evidence at best, not an anchor, and unused. (4) annulment - all three concur it is negligible. JUDGMENT dispute, unresolved by evidence: plateau vs continued narrowing. Run 2 reads the flat window-means as a plateau; I weight the within-house series instead, because window-means confound composition and four independent houses each drifted 1-2 pp toward Flavio over the same fortnight. That is the bet I would take, so I apply a small residual drift and land at -0.5, just below all three runs rather than between them. Second unresolved item: which house publishes first on Sep 17-18 cannot be determined - the Thursday slot weakly suggests PoderData/Aya (-1) but Datafolha (+2) also released on a Thursday. I leave that as width rather than guessing, which is why the 10-90 stays at 7.1 pp. Escape masses carried forward at the runs' consensus 0.06 low / 0.005 high; the low-side mechanism (Verita/Gerp-class print past -6) is concrete and recently observed.
